pr_body:
Motivation:

Exception occurs in the MQTT message builder class (`io.netty.handler.codec.mqtt.MqttMessageBuilders`) when trying to create a message with packetId > 32767

Modification:

refactor the `short` packetId into `int`
as the underlying `MqttMessageIdVariableHeader` of the message treats it as an `int` anyway.

Result:
see unit-test: `MqttMessageBuildersPacketIdTest`

Fixes #10929 .
pr_comment:
it looks like changing the function signature is not allowed.
I could refactor it so that the builder functions still take a `short`, but in my opinion it makes more sense to align this with the underlying _variable header_ (which takes an `int`) ?

@normanmaurer I changed it back again to take the `packetId` in as a `short`.
But wouldn't it be more generic to actually change that API to work with an `int` (as is done in other mqtt-message methods)?
Now you will always have to convert between `int` and `short` whenever you use these builders.

Or is it an option to define both and mark the ones that take in a `short` as _deprecated_ ?

Anyway, this PR should solve the issue now that a `packetId` > 32767 would result in a negative one when pushed through these builder classes.
@duke-bartholomew I was actually suggesting that you add the `int` methods but keep the short as well.
@normanmaurer sorry about the misunderstanding ... new commit adds them back (and deprecates the ones that take in a `short`)
